docs.title: Image Compression Strategy
docs.text:
class ImageOptimizer {
  static Future<File> optimizeForClassification(File originalFile) async {
    final bytes = await originalFile.readAsBytes();
    final image = img.decodeImage(bytes);

    if (image == null) throw Exception('Invalid image');

    // Resize to model input size
    final resized = img.copyResize(
      image,
      width: 224,
      height: 224,
      interpolation: img.Interpolation.cubic,
    );

    // Compress with optimal quality
    final compressed = img.encodeJpg(resized, quality: 90);

    // Save to temporary file
    final tempDir = await getTemporaryDirectory();
    final tempFile = File('${tempDir.path}/optimized_${DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch}.jpg');
    await tempFile.writeAsBytes(compressed);

    return tempFile;
  }

  static Future<void> cleanupTempFiles() async {
    final tempDir = await getTemporaryDirectory();
    final files = tempDir.listSync();

    for (final file in files) {
      if (file.path.contains('optimized_')) {
        await file.delete();
      }
    }
  }
}

class CachedApiClient {
  static final Map<String, CacheEntry> _cache = {};
  static const Duration _cacheTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5);

  static Future<Map<String, dynamic>> getCachedResponse(
    String url,
    Map<String, String> headers,
  ) async {
    final cacheKey = _generateCacheKey(url, headers);
    final cached = _cache[cacheKey];

    if (cached != null && !cached.isExpired) {
      return cached.data;
    }

    final response = await http.get(Uri.parse(url), headers: headers);
    final data = json.decode(response.body);

    _cache[cacheKey] = CacheEntry(data, DateTime.now().add(_cacheTimeout));
    return data;
  }

  static String _generateCacheKey(String url, Map<String, String> headers) {
    return '$url${headers.toString()}';
  }
}

class CacheEntry {
  final Map<String, dynamic> data;
  final DateTime expiry;

  CacheEntry(this.data, this.expiry);

  bool get isExpired => DateTime.now().isAfter(expiry);
}

class OptimizedMosquitoRepository {
  final DatabaseService _databaseService;

  // Use prepared statements and indexes
  Future<List<MosquitoSpecies>> getSpeciesByRegion(String region) async {
    final db = await _databaseService.database;

    // Use parameterized queries
    final results = await db.query(
      'mosquito_species',
      where: 'distribution LIKE ? AND active = 1',
      whereArgs: ['%$region%'],
      orderBy: 'name ASC',
      limit: 50, // Limit results for performance
    );

    return results.map((row) => MosquitoSpecies.fromMap(row)).toList();
  }

  // Batch operations for better performance
  Future<void> insertSpeciesBatch(List<MosquitoSpecies> species) async {
    final db = await _databaseService.database;
    final batch = db.batch();

    for (final species in species) {
      batch.insert('mosquito_species', species.toMap());
    }

    await batch.commit(noResult: true);
  }
}

class MainActivity: FlutterActivity() {

    override fun onTrimMemory(level: Int) {
        super.onTrimMemory(level)

        // Clear caches when memory is low
        when (level) {
            TRIM_MEMORY_RUNNING_CRITICAL,
            TRIM_MEMORY_COMPLETE -> {
                // Clear image caches
                MethodChannel(flutterEngine!!.dartExecutor.binaryMessenger, "memory")
                    .invokeMethod("clearCaches", null)
            }
        }

}

class PerformanceMonitor {
  static final Map<String, List<int>> _metrics = {};

  static void recordInferenceTime(int milliseconds) {
    _metrics.putIfAbsent('inference_time', () => []).add(milliseconds);
  }

  static void recordMemoryUsage(int bytes) {
    _metrics.putIfAbsent('memory_usage', () => []).add(bytes);
  }

  static Map<String, double> getAverageMetrics() {
    final averages = <String, double>{};

    _metrics.forEach((key, values) {
      if (values.isNotEmpty) {
        averages[key] = values.reduce((a, b) => a + b) / values.length;
      }
    });

    return averages;
  }

  static void clearMetrics() {
    _metrics.clear();
  }
}

docs.title: Import Organization
docs.text:
Organize imports in the following order with blank lines between groups:

// 1. Dart core libraries
import 'dart:async';

// 2. Flutter framework

docs.title: Class Structure
docs.text:
Organize class members in the following order:

class ExampleClass {
  // 1. Static constants
  static const String CONSTANT_VALUE = 'value';

  // 2. Instance variables (private first, then public)
  final String _privateField;
  final String publicField;

  // 3. Constructor
  ExampleClass({
    required this.publicField,
    String? privateField,
  }) : _privateField = privateField ?? 'default';

  // 4. Getters and setters
  String get privateField => _privateField;

  // 5. Public methods
  void publicMethod() { }

  // 6. Private methods
  void _privateMethod() { }

  // 7. Override methods
  @override
  String toString() => 'ExampleClass($_privateField)';
}

docs.title: Method Organization
docs.text:
• Keep methods focused and single-purpose
  • Use descriptive names that explain what the method does
  • Limit method length to ~50 lines when possible
  • Extract complex logic into private helper methods
// Good: Descriptive and focused
Future<ClassificationResult> classifyMosquitoImage(File imageFile) async {
  final processedImage = await _preprocessImage(imageFile);
  final prediction = await _runModelInference(processedImage);
  return _parseClassificationResult(prediction);
}

// Helper methods for complex operations
Future<Uint8List> _preprocessImage(File imageFile) async { }
Future<List<double>> _runModelInference(Uint8List imageData) async { }
ClassificationResult _parseClassificationResult(List<double> output) { }

docs.text: The project follows the official Dart Style Guide with these specific conventions:

docs.title: Line Length

docs.text:
• Use flutter format . to automatically format code
  • Enable "Format on Save" in your IDE
  • Use trailing commas for better diffs and formatting
// Good: Trailing commas and proper formatting
Widget build(BuildContext context) {

docs.title: Documentation Comments
docs.text:
Use dartdoc comments for public APIs:

/// Classifies a mosquito image using the trained PyTorch model.
///
/// Takes an [imageFile] and returns a [ClassificationResult] containing
/// the predicted species and confidence score. Throws [ClassificationException]
/// if the image cannot be processed.
///
/// Example:
/// ```dart
/// final result = await classifyMosquitoImage(imageFile);
/// print('Species: ${result.species}, Confidence: ${result.confidence}');
/// ```
Future<ClassificationResult> classifyMosquitoImage(File imageFile) async {
  // Implementation
}

docs.title: Exception Handling
docs.text:
• Use specific exception types when possible
  • Provide meaningful error messages
  • Log errors appropriately for debugging
try {
  final result = await classificationService.classify(image);
  return result;
} on ClassificationException catch (e) {
  logger.error('Classification failed: ${e.message}');
  throw ClassificationException('Unable to classify image: ${e.message}');
} catch (e) {
  logger.error('Unexpected error during classification: $e');
  throw Exception('An unexpected error occurred');
}

docs.title: Null Safety
docs.text:
• Use null safety features effectively
  • Prefer non-nullable types when possible
  • Use null-aware operators appropriately
// Good: Clear null handling
String? getUserName() {
  return user?.name?.trim().isEmpty == true ? null : user?.name?.trim();
}

// Better: Using null-aware operators
String? getUserName() => user?.name?.trim().nullIfEmpty;

docs.title: Provider Pattern
docs.text:
• Use ChangeNotifier for simple state management
  • Implement proper disposal of resources
  • Use Consumer widgets for targeted rebuilds
class ClassificationViewModel extends ChangeNotifier {
  bool _isClassifying = false;
  ClassificationResult? _result;

  bool get isClassifying => _isClassifying;
  ClassificationResult? get result => _result;

  Future<void> classifyImage(File image) async {
    _isClassifying = true;
    notifyListeners();

    try {
      _result = await _repository.classifyImage(image);
    } finally {
      _isClassifying = false;
      notifyListeners();
    }
  }

  @override
  void dispose() {
    // Clean up resources
    super.dispose();
  }
}

docs.title: Test File Organization
docs.text:
• Mirror the lib/ structure in test/
  • Use _test.dart suffix for test files
  • Group related tests using group() function
// test/unit/services/classification_service_test.dart
void main() {
  group('ClassificationService', () {
    late ClassificationService service;

    setUp(() {
      service = ClassificationService();
    });

    group('classifyImage', () {
      test('should return valid result for valid image', () async {
        // Test implementation
      });

      test('should throw exception for invalid image', () async {
        // Test implementation
      });
    });
  });
}

test('should return Aedes aegypti when image contains yellow fever mosquito', () {
  // Test implementation
});

test('should throw ClassificationException when image is corrupted', () {
  // Test implementation
});

docs.title: Memory Management

  • Use const constructors when possible
  • Avoid memory leaks in long-lived objects

docs.title: Image Handling

  • Cache processed images appropriately
  • Dispose of image resources after use

docs.title: Database Operations

  • Implement proper indexing for queries
  • Close database connections properly

docs.title: Data Protection

  • Use secure storage for sensitive information
  • Validate all user inputs

docs.title: API Security

{

docs.text:
• feature/description for new features
  • bugfix/description for bug fixes
  • hotfix/description for urgent fixes
  • docs/description for documentation updates

docs.title: Commit Messages
docs.text:
Follow conventional commit format: 

type(scope): description

[optional body]

[optional footer]

Examples:

fix(database): resolve migration issue for disease table
docs(api): update classification service documentation

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: Following these conventions ensures consistency, maintainability, and collaboration effectiveness across the CulicidaeLab project. When in doubt, refer to the official Dart and Flutter style guides, and maintain consistency with existing code patterns in the project.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: This guide provides comprehensive instructions for setting up a development environment for the CulicidaeLab Flutter mobile application. The project supports both containerized development using VS Code Dev Containers and manual local setup.

docs.title: System Requirements
docs.text:
• Operating System: Windows 10/11, macOS 10.14+, or Ubuntu 18.04+
  • RAM: Minimum 8GB, recommended 16GB
  • Storage: At least 10GB free space for development tools and dependencies
  • Network: Stable internet connection for downloading dependencies

docs.title: Required Tools
docs.text:
• Git: Version control system
  • VS Code: Recommended IDE with Flutter extensions
  • Docker: For containerized development (optional but recommended)

docs.title: Option 1: Dev Container Setup (Recommended)
docs.text: The easiest way to get started is using the provided Dev Container configuration, which provides a consistent development environment across all platforms.

docs.title: Prerequisites for Dev Container
docs.text:
1. Install Docker Desktop
  2. Windows: Download from Docker Desktop for Windows
  3. macOS: Download from Docker Desktop for Mac

  4. Linux: Follow Docker Engine installation guide

  5. Install VS Code

  6. Download from Visual Studio Code

  7. Install Dev Containers Extension

  8. Open VS Code
  9. Go to Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X)
  10. Search for "Dev Containers" by Microsoft
  11. Install the extension

docs.title: Setting Up Dev Container
docs.text:
1. Clone the Repository 

    git clone https://github.com/your-org/culicidaelab.git
cd culicidaelab

  2. Open in Dev Container

  3. Open VS Code
  4. Open the project folder
  5. VS Code should detect the .devcontainer configuration

  6. Click "Reopen in Container" when prompted, or:

    • Press Ctrl+Shift+P (Cmd+Shift+P on Mac)
    • Type "Dev Containers: Reopen in Container"
    • Select the command

  7. Wait for Container Build

  8. The first build may take 10-15 minutes
  9. Subsequent starts will be much faster

  10. The container includes:

    • Flutter SDK 3.29.3
    • Android SDK with Platform 35
    • Android Build Tools 34.0.0
    • Android NDK 27.0.12077973
    • Java 17
    • All necessary development tools

  11. Verify Installation 

    flutter doctor

  12. This should show all checkmarks for Android development
  13. iOS development will show as unavailable (expected on Linux container)

docs.title: Dev Container Features
docs.text:
The dev container includes:

  • Pre-configured Flutter SDK: Latest stable version with Android support
  • Android Development Tools: Complete Android SDK, NDK, and build tools
  • VS Code Extensions: Flutter, Dart, and helpful development extensions
  • USB Device Support: Physical device debugging capabilities
  • Port Forwarding: Automatic port forwarding for development servers

// test/unit/view_models/classification_view_model_test.dart
import 'package:flutter_test/flutter_test.dart';
import 'package:mockito/mockito.dart';
import 'package:mockito/annotations.dart';

@GenerateMocks([ClassificationRepository, UserService])
import 'classification_view_model_test.mocks.dart';

void main() {
  group('ClassificationViewModel', () {
    late ClassificationViewModel viewModel;
    late MockClassificationRepository mockRepository;
    late MockUserService mockUserService;

    setUp(() {
      mockRepository = MockClassificationRepository();
      mockUserService = MockUserService();
      viewModel = ClassificationViewModel(
        repository: mockRepository,
        userService: mockUserService,
      );
    });

    tearDown(() {
      viewModel.dispose();
    });

    group('Initial State', () {
      test('should start with correct initial state', () {
        expect(viewModel.state, ClassificationState.initial);
        expect(viewModel.hasImage, false);
        expect(viewModel.result, null);
        expect(viewModel.errorMessage, null);
      });
    });

    group('Image Classification', () {
      test('should update state during classification process', () async {
        // Arrange
        final testFile = File('test_image.jpg');
        final expectedResult = ClassificationResult(
          species: createTestSpecies(),
          confidence: 95.0,
          inferenceTime: 150,
          relatedDiseases: [],
          imageFile: testFile,
        );

        when(mockRepository.classifyImage(any, any))
            .thenAnswer((_) async => expectedResult);

        viewModel.setImageFile(testFile);

        // Act & Assert
        expect(viewModel.state, ClassificationState.initial);

        final future = viewModel.classifyImage(MockAppLocalizations());
        expect(viewModel.state, ClassificationState.loading);

        await future;
        expect(viewModel.state, ClassificationState.success);
        expect(viewModel.result, expectedResult);
      });

      test('should handle classification errors gracefully', () async {
        // Arrange
        when(mockRepository.classifyImage(any, any))
            .thenThrow(Exception('Network error'));

        viewModel.setImageFile(File('test_image.jpg'));

        // Act
        await viewModel.classifyImage(MockAppLocalizations());

        // Assert
        expect(viewModel.state, ClassificationState.error);
        expect(viewModel.errorMessage, contains('Classification failed'));
        expect(viewModel.result, null);
      });
    });
  });
}

// test/ai/model_validation_test.dart
void main() {
  group('AI Model Validation', () {
    late ClassificationService service;

    setUpAll(() async {
      service = ClassificationService(pytorchWrapper: PytorchWrapper());
      await service.loadModel();
    });

    group('Model Accuracy Tests', () {
      test('should classify known species correctly', () async {
        final testCases = [
          TestCase('aedes_aegypti_1.jpg', 'Aedes aegypti', minConfidence: 0.8),
          TestCase('anopheles_gambiae_1.jpg', 'Anopheles gambiae', minConfidence: 0.7),
          TestCase('culex_pipiens_1.jpg', 'Culex pipiens', minConfidence: 0.75),
        ];

        for (final testCase in testCases) {
          final image = File('test/fixtures/species/${testCase.imagePath}');
          final result = await service.classifyImage(image);

          expect(
            result['scientificName'],
            testCase.expectedSpecies,
            reason: 'Failed for ${testCase.imagePath}',
          );
          expect(
            result['confidence'],
            greaterThanOrEqualTo(testCase.minConfidence),
            reason: 'Low confidence for ${testCase.imagePath}',
          );
        }
      });

      test('should handle edge cases appropriately', () async {
        final edgeCases = [
          'blurry_mosquito.jpg',
          'partial_mosquito.jpg',
          'multiple_mosquitoes.jpg',
          'no_mosquito.jpg',
        ];

        for (final imagePath in edgeCases) {
          final image = File('test/fixtures/edge_cases/$imagePath');
          final result = await service.classifyImage(image);

          // Should not crash and should return valid result structure
          expect(result, contains('scientificName'));
          expect(result, contains('confidence'));
          expect(result['confidence'], inInclusiveRange(0.0, 1.0));
        }
      });
    });

    group('Model Performance Tests', () {
      test('should meet inference time requirements', () async {
        final testImage = File('test/fixtures/test_mosquito.jpg');
        final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();

        await service.classifyImage(testImage);

        stopwatch.stop();
        expect(
          stopwatch.elapsedMilliseconds,
          lessThan(5000), // Should complete within 5 seconds
        );
      });

      test('should handle batch processing efficiently', () async {
        final images = List.generate(
          10,
          (i) => File('test/fixtures/batch/mosquito_$i.jpg'),
        );

        final stopwatch = Stopwatch()..start();

        for (final image in images) {
          await service.classifyImage(image);
        }

        stopwatch.stop();
        final avgTime = stopwatch.elapsedMilliseconds / images.length;

        expect(avgTime, lessThan(2000)); // Average under 2 seconds per image
      });
    });
  });
}

class TestCase {
  final String imagePath;
  final String expectedSpecies;
  final double minConfidence;

  TestCase(this.imagePath, this.expectedSpecies, {required this.minConfidence});
}

// test/performance/classification_performance_test.dart
void main() {
  group('Classification Performance Tests', () {
    late ClassificationViewModel viewModel;
    late List<File> testImages;

    setUpAll(() async {
      viewModel = ClassificationViewModel(
        repository: ClassificationRepository(),
        userService: UserService(),
      );
      await viewModel.initModel(TestLocalizations());

      testImages = await loadTestImages();
    });

    testWidgets('should meet performance benchmarks', (tester) async {
      final results = <PerformanceResult>[];

      for (final image in testImages) {
        final result = await measurePerformance(
          'Image Classification',
          () async {
            viewModel.setImageFile(image);
            await viewModel.classifyImage(TestLocalizations());
            return viewModel.result;
          },
        );

        results.add(result);
      }

      // Analyze results
      final avgInferenceTime = results
          .map((r) => r.duration)
          .reduce((a, b) => a + b) / results.length;

      expect(avgInferenceTime, lessThan(3000)); // Average under 3 seconds

      // Check for performance regressions
      final maxTime = results.map((r) => r.duration).reduce(math.max);
      expect(maxTime, lessThan(10000)); // No single inference over 10 seconds
    });

    testWidgets('should handle memory efficiently', (tester) async {
      final initialMemory = await getMemoryUsage();

      // Process multiple images
      for (int i = 0; i < 20; i++) {
        final image = testImages[i % testImages.length];
        viewModel.setImageFile(image);
        await viewModel.classifyImage(TestLocalizations());
        viewModel.reset(); // Simulate user resetting
      }

      // Force garbage collection
      await Future.delayed(Duration(seconds: 1));

      final finalMemory = await getMemoryUsage();
      final memoryIncrease = finalMemory - initialMemory;

      // Memory increase should be reasonable (less than 100MB)
      expect(memoryIncrease, lessThan(100 * 1024 * 1024));
    });
  });
}

// test/utils/test_image_utils.dart
class TestImageUtils {
  static const String testImagesPath = 'test/fixtures/images';

  static Future<List<File>> loadTestImages() async {
    final directory = Directory(testImagesPath);
    if (!directory.existsSync()) {
      throw Exception('Test images directory not found: $testImagesPath');
    }

    return directory
        .listSync()
        .where((entity) => entity is File && entity.path.endsWith('.jpg'))
        .map((entity) => File(entity.path))
        .toList();
  }

  static Uint8List createTestImageBytes({
    int width = 224,
    int height = 224,
  }) {
    // Create a simple test image
    final image = img.Image(width: width, height: height);
    img.fill(image, color: img.ColorRgb8(128, 128, 128));
    return Uint8List.fromList(img.encodeJpg(image));
  }

  static Future<File> createTempTestImage() async {
    final tempDir = await getTemporaryDirectory();
    final file = File('${tempDir.path}/test_image_${DateTime.now().millisecondsSinceEpoch}.jpg');
    await file.writeAsBytes(createTestImageBytes());
    return file;
  }
}

// scripts/test_quality_gates.dart
void main(List<String> args) {
  final coverageFile = File('coverage/lcov.info');
  if (!coverageFile.existsSync()) {
    print('Coverage file not found');
    exit(1);
  }

  final coverage = parseCoverageFile(coverageFile);

  // Enforce minimum coverage thresholds
  if (coverage.lineCoverage < 80.0) {
    print('Line coverage ${coverage.lineCoverage}% is below threshold (80%)');
    exit(1);
  }

  if (coverage.branchCoverage < 70.0) {
    print('Branch coverage ${coverage.branchCoverage}% is below threshold (70%)');
    exit(1);
  }

  print('All quality gates passed!');
  print('Line coverage: ${coverage.lineCoverage}%');
  print('Branch coverage: ${coverage.branchCoverage}%');
}

docs.title: Disease Information Guide
docs.text: Learn about mosquito-borne diseases, their symptoms, prevention methods, and how to use CulicidaeLab's disease information features effectively.

docs.title: Understanding Mosquito-Borne Diseases
docs.text: Mosquito-borne diseases are illnesses transmitted to humans through the bites of infected mosquitoes. These diseases represent a significant global health challenge, affecting millions of people worldwide.

docs.title: How Disease Transmission Works
docs.text:
The Vector-Pathogen-Host Cycle 1. Pathogen: Virus, parasite, or bacteria that causes disease 2. Vector: Mosquito species that can carry and transmit the pathogen 3. Host: Humans or animals that can be infected 4. Environment: Conditions that support mosquito breeding and pathogen development

Transmission Process 1. Mosquito bites an infected person or animal 2. Pathogen enters the mosquito and develops 3. Infected mosquito bites a healthy person 4. Pathogen is transmitted to the new host 5. Disease develops in the newly infected person

docs.title: Major Disease Categories
docs.text:
Viral Diseases - Dengue Fever - Zika Virus Disease - Chikungunya - Yellow Fever - West Nile Virus

Parasitic Diseases - Malaria - Lymphatic Filariasis

Bacterial Diseases - Some forms of encephalitis

docs.title: Accessing Disease Information
docs.text:
From the Main Menu 1. Tap the hospital icon (🏥) in the bottom navigation 2. Browse the complete list of mosquito-borne diseases 3. Use the search function to find specific diseases

From Classification Results 1. After identifying a mosquito, tap "Disease Risks" 2. View diseases specifically associated with that species 3. Tap on any disease for detailed information

From Species Gallery 1. Open any species detail page 2. Scroll to the "Associated Diseases" section 3. Tap on disease names for full information

docs.title: Disease Information Layout
docs.text:
Each disease entry provides comprehensive information:

Overview Section - Disease name in your selected language - High-quality illustration or microscopic image - Brief description of the disease - Causative agent (virus, parasite, or bacteria)

Transmission Information - Vector species that transmit the disease - Geographic distribution and prevalence - Seasonal patterns and risk periods - Transmission requirements and conditions

Clinical Information - Common symptoms and their progression - Incubation period (time from infection to symptoms) - Disease severity and potential complications - Diagnostic methods and testing

Prevention and Treatment - Personal protection measures - Environmental control methods - Available vaccines (if any) - Treatment options and medical care - When to seek medical attention

docs.title: Search and Filter Features
docs.text:
Search Functionality - Search by disease name - Search by symptoms - Search by vector species - Search by geographic region

Filter Options - Filter by disease severity - Filter by availability of vaccines - Filter by geographic relevance - Filter by vector species## Major Mosquito-Borne Diseases

docs.title: Dengue Fever
docs.text: Overview: Most widespread mosquito-borne viral disease globally - Vectors: Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus - Symptoms: High fever, severe headache, muscle pain, skin rash - Geographic Range: Tropical and subtropical regions worldwide - Prevention: Eliminate standing water, use repellents, wear protective clothing - Treatment: Supportive care, pain relief, fluid replacement

docs.title: Zika Virus Disease
docs.text: Overview: Viral disease with serious implications for pregnant women - Vectors: Primarily Aedes aegypti - Symptoms: Often mild or asymptomatic; fever, rash, joint pain - Special Concerns: Birth defects when contracted during pregnancy - Geographic Range: Americas, Africa, Asia, Pacific Islands - Prevention: Especially important for pregnant women and those planning pregnancy

docs.title: Chikungunya
docs.text: Overview: Viral disease causing severe joint pain - Vectors: Aedes aegypti, Aedes albopictus - Symptoms: Sudden onset fever, severe joint pain, muscle pain, rash - Characteristic: Joint pain can persist for months or years - Geographic Range: Africa, Asia, Europe, Americas - Prevention: Similar to dengue prevention methods

docs.title: Yellow Fever
docs.text: Overview: Viral disease with potential for severe complications - Vectors: Aedes aegypti (urban), forest mosquitoes (sylvatic) - Symptoms: Fever, headache, jaundice, bleeding - Severity: Can be fatal in severe cases - Prevention: Highly effective vaccine available - Geographic Range: Tropical Africa and South America

docs.title: Malaria
docs.text: Overview: Parasitic disease and leading cause of mosquito-borne deaths - Vectors: Anopheles species mosquitoes - Symptoms: Fever, chills, sweats, headache, fatigue - Severity: Can be fatal if untreated - Geographic Range: Tropical and subtropical regions - Prevention: Bed nets, antimalarial medications, vector control

docs.title: West Nile Virus
docs.text: Overview: Viral disease common in temperate regions - Vectors: Culex species mosquitoes - Symptoms: Often asymptomatic; fever, headache, body aches - Severe Cases: Neurological complications possible - Geographic Range: Africa, Europe, Middle East, North America - Prevention: Personal protection, especially during peak mosquito season

docs.title: Personal Protection
docs.text:
Clothing and Barriers - Wear long-sleeved shirts and long pants - Use light-colored clothing (mosquitoes are attracted to dark colors) - Treat clothing with permethrin insecticide - Use bed nets, especially in high-risk areas

Repellents - Use EPA-registered insect repellents - DEET, picaridin, IR3535, and oil of lemon eucalyptus are effective - Apply according to label instructions - Reapply as directed, especially after swimming or sweating

Environmental Modifications - Remove standing water around homes - Clean gutters and drainage systems - Cover water storage containers - Maintain swimming pools and water features

docs.title: Community Prevention
docs.text:
Vector Control Programs - Support local mosquito control efforts - Report mosquito breeding sites to authorities - Participate in community clean-up activities - Advocate for effective public health measures

Surveillance and Monitoring - Report unusual mosquito activity - Participate in disease surveillance programs - Support research and monitoring efforts - Stay informed about local disease risks

docs.title: Warning Signs
docs.text: Seek immediate medical attention if you experience: - High fever (over 101°F/38.3°C) - Severe headache or neck stiffness - Persistent vomiting - Difficulty breathing - Severe abdominal pain - Bleeding or bruising - Confusion or altered mental state

docs.title: Special Populations
docs.text:
Pregnant Women - Increased risk from Zika virus - Consult healthcare providers about travel to affected areas - Take extra precautions against mosquito bites - Seek immediate care for any fever or symptoms

Immunocompromised Individuals - Higher risk of severe disease - May need additional preventive measures - Consult healthcare providers about specific risks - Consider avoiding high-risk areas during outbreaks

Travelers - Research disease risks at destination - Consult travel medicine specialists - Consider prophylactic medications where appropriate - Maintain prevention measures throughout travel

docs.title: Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ)
docs.text: Find answers to the most common questions about CulicidaeLab, its features, and how to use the app effectively.

docs.title: What is CulicidaeLab?
docs.text: CulicidaeLab is a mobile application that uses artificial intelligence to identify mosquito species from photographs. It also provides comprehensive information about mosquito-borne diseases and serves as an educational tool for public health awareness and scientific research.

docs.title: Is CulicidaeLab free to use?
docs.text: Yes, CulicidaeLab is completely free to download and use. There are no in-app purchases, subscriptions, or hidden fees. The app is supported by research grants and is designed to serve the public good.

docs.title: What devices are supported?
docs.text: Android: Version 5.0 (API Level 21) or newer with at least 3GB RAM iOS: Version 12.0 or newer with at least 3GB RAM Not Supported: Web browsers, Windows, macOS, or Linux desktop applications

docs.title: Do I need internet to use the app?
docs.text: For Identification: No, the AI model runs entirely on your device For Gallery and Diseases: Initial download requires internet, then works offline For Map and Observations: Internet connection required For Updates: Internet needed for app updates and new content

docs.title: How accurate is the mosquito identification?
docs.text: The AI model achieves over 90% accuracy for the most common disease-vector mosquito species. Accuracy depends on photo quality, lighting conditions, and the species being identified. Always verify results using the species gallery and consider geographic distribution.

docs.title: How does the AI identification work?
docs.text: CulicidaeLab uses a deep learning neural network (PyTorch Lite) trained on thousands of mosquito images from scientific collections. The model analyzes visual features like body patterns, wing structure, and size proportions to identify species.

docs.title: What mosquito species can the app identify?
docs.text: The app can identify the most epidemiologically significant mosquito species, focusing on those that transmit diseases to humans. This includes species from genera like Aedes, Anopheles, and Culex. The exact number of species varies by app version.

docs.title: Why do I get different results for the same mosquito?
docs.text: Several factors can cause variation: - Photo Quality: Different lighting, angles, or focus - Image Processing: Slight variations in how the AI processes images - Mosquito Condition: Damage, positioning, or life stage - Model Uncertainty: Some species are more difficult to distinguish

docs.title: What should I do if the identification seems wrong?
docs.text:
1. Check Photo Quality: Ensure clear, well-lit images
  2. Try Multiple Photos: Take several photos from different angles
  3. Compare with Gallery: Verify against species images and descriptions
  4. Check Geographic Range: Ensure the species occurs in your location
  5. Consider Confidence Score: Lower scores indicate less certainty

docs.title: Can the app identify mosquito larvae or eggs?
docs.text: No, the current version only identifies adult mosquitoes. The AI model is trained specifically on adult mosquito morphology and cannot accurately identify larvae, pupae, or eggs.

docs.title: What data does the app collect?
docs.text:
Automatically Collected: - Device type and operating system version - App usage statistics (anonymous) - Crash reports and error logs

User-Provided (optional): - Photos you choose to analyze - Location data for observations (if you submit them) - Notes and comments for observations

docs.title: Is my personal information safe?
docs.text: Yes, CulicidaeLab is designed with privacy in mind: - No Personal Information: We don't collect names, emails, or personal details - Anonymous Usage: All usage data is anonymized - Local Processing: AI identification happens on your device - Optional Sharing: You choose what observations to submit

docs.title: Are my photos stored or shared?
docs.text: Local Storage: Photos are temporarily stored on your device for processing Not Uploaded: Photos are not automatically uploaded to servers User Choice: You can choose to include photos when submitting observations Deletion: You can delete photos from the app at any time

docs.title: Can I use the app without sharing any data?
docs.text: Yes, you can use all core features (identification, gallery, disease info) without sharing any data. Only the map feature and observation submission require data sharing, and both are optional.

docs.title: Why is the app so large?
docs.text: The app includes: - AI Model: Neural network files (~50-100MB) - Species Database: Images and information for all species - Disease Database: Comprehensive disease information - Multi-language Content: Text in multiple languages - Offline Capability: All content available without internet

docs.title: Why does the app take time to load initially?
docs.text: On first launch, the app needs to: - Load AI Model: Initialize the neural network - Cache Images: Download species and disease images - Set Up Database: Prepare local data storage - Configure Languages: Set up localization

docs.title: Can I use the app on multiple devices?
docs.text: Yes, you can install CulicidaeLab on multiple devices. However: - No Sync: Data doesn't sync between devices - Separate Setup: Each device needs individual setup - Independent Usage: Each installation works independently

docs.title: How often is the app updated?
docs.text: Regular Updates: New versions released every 2-3 months Content Updates: Species and disease information updated regularly Model Improvements: AI model updated as new training data becomes available Bug Fixes: Critical issues addressed in patch releases

docs.title: Is CulicidaeLab scientifically accurate?
docs.text: Yes, the app is developed with scientific rigor: - Expert Review: Content reviewed by entomologists and public health experts - Scientific Sources: Information based on peer-reviewed research - Continuous Updates: Regular updates based on latest scientific findings - Quality Control: Rigorous testing and validation processes

docs.title: Can I use CulicidaeLab for research?
docs.text:
Yes, the app supports research activities: - Citizen Science: Contribute observations to research databases - Educational Use: Suitable for teaching and learning - Field Work: Useful for preliminary species identification - Data Collection: Submit observations with location and metadata

Important: For formal research, always verify identifications with expert taxonomists.

docs.title: How can I contribute to improving the app?
docs.text: Submit Observations: Share high-quality observations with location data Report Issues: Report bugs, errors, or suggestions for improvement Provide Feedback: Share your experience and suggestions Educational Outreach: Help others learn about mosquito-borne diseases Scientific Collaboration: Researchers can contact the development team

docs.title: Can teachers use this app in classrooms?
docs.text: Absolutely! CulicidaeLab is excellent for education: - Biology Classes: Learn about insect morphology and taxonomy - Public Health: Understand disease vectors and prevention - Environmental Science: Explore human-environment interactions - Technology: Demonstrate AI and machine learning applications

docs.title: The app crashes frequently. What should I do?
docs.text:
Immediate Solutions: 1. Restart the app completely 2. Restart your device 3. Clear app cache 4. Update to the latest version 5. Free up device storage space

If Problems Persist: See our detailed Troubleshooting Guide

docs.title: Why can't I take photos?
docs.text: Check Permissions: Ensure camera access is enabled in device settings Camera Conflicts: Close other apps that might be using the camera Hardware Issues: Test camera in other apps to verify it's working App Updates: Update to the latest version

docs.title: The identification is very slow. How can I speed it up?
docs.text:
Device Optimization: - Close other running apps - Restart your device - Ensure adequate free storage - Use smaller image files - Allow device to cool if overheated

Photo Optimization: - Use well-lit, clear photos - Avoid extremely large image files - Ensure mosquito is clearly visible

docs.title: Why don't I see all the species mentioned in documentation?
docs.text: Regional Differences: Species availability may vary by geographic region App Version: Older versions may have fewer species Language Settings: Some species names may vary by language Updates: New species added in app updates

docs.title: How do I report a bug or problem?
docs.text: In-App Reporting: Use any feedback features within the app App Store Reviews: Leave detailed reviews in Google Play or App Store Official Channels: Contact through official website or email Community Forums: Report issues in user communities

docs.title: How do I suggest new features?
docs.text: User Feedback: Use in-app feedback mechanisms Community Discussion: Participate in user forums and discussions Direct Contact: Reach out through official communication channels Academic Collaboration: Researchers can propose collaborative features

docs.text: Yes! Comprehensive documentation is available: - Getting Started: Getting Started Guide - Identification Help: Mosquito Identification Guide - Gallery Usage: Using Gallery Guide - Disease Information: Disease Information Guide - Technical Issues: Troubleshooting Guide

docs.title: Can I get training on using the app?
docs.text: Self-Guided Learning: Use the comprehensive guides and in-app help Educational Resources: Access teaching materials and presentations Community Support: Join user communities and discussion groups Professional Training: Contact the development team for institutional training

docs.title: Can I use this app for medical diagnosis?
docs.text: No, CulicidaeLab is for educational and research purposes only. It should never be used for medical diagnosis or treatment decisions. Always consult healthcare professionals for medical concerns.

docs.title: What should I do if I think I've been bitten by a disease-carrying mosquito?
docs.text:
1. Monitor Symptoms: Watch for fever, headache, or other symptoms
  2. Seek Medical Care: Consult healthcare professionals if symptoms develop
  3. Provide Information: Share mosquito identification with healthcare providers
  4. Follow Medical Advice: Follow professional medical guidance
  5. Report to Authorities: Consider reporting to local health departments

docs.title: Is the disease information medically accurate?
docs.text:
Yes, disease information is based on authoritative sources like WHO and CDC, but it's for educational purposes only. Always consult healthcare professionals for medical advice and current treatment guidelines.

Still have questions?

docs.title: Mosquito Identification Guide
docs.text: Learn how to effectively use CulicidaeLab's AI-powered mosquito identification feature to get accurate species identification results.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: CulicidaeLab uses advanced machine learning technology to identify mosquito species from photographs. The app analyzes visual features like body patterns, wing structure, and size proportions to determine the most likely species.

docs.title: The AI Model
docs.text:
• Technology: PyTorch Lite neural network optimized for mobile devices
  • Training Data: Thousands of mosquito images from scientific collections
  • Accuracy: Over 90% accuracy for the most common disease-vector species
  • Processing: All analysis happens on your device - no internet required for identification

docs.title: Taking Effective Photos
docs.text: The quality of your photo directly impacts identification accuracy. Follow these guidelines for best results:

docs.title: Lighting Conditions
docs.text:
• Natural Light: Use bright, natural daylight when possible
  • Avoid Flash: Flash can create harsh shadows and overexpose details
  • Even Lighting: Ensure the mosquito is evenly lit without strong shadows
  • Avoid Backlighting: Don't photograph with bright light behind the mosquito

docs.title: Camera Distance and Focus
docs.text:
• Close-up: Get as close as possible while maintaining focus
  • Fill the Frame: The mosquito should occupy most of the image
  • Sharp Focus: Ensure the mosquito is in sharp focus, especially the body and wings
  • Steady Hands: Hold the camera steady or use a tripod for sharp images

docs.title: Mosquito Positioning
docs.text:
• Dorsal View: Top-down view showing the back and wings is ideal
  • Full Body: Include the entire mosquito from head to abdomen
  • Wings Spread: If possible, capture with wings spread for better identification
  • Avoid Partial Views: Don't crop off important body parts

docs.title: Background and Composition
docs.text:
• Plain Background: Use a simple, contrasting background
  • Avoid Clutter: Remove distracting objects from the frame
  • Contrast: Ensure good contrast between the mosquito and background
  • Stable Surface: Place the mosquito on a stable, flat surface if possible

docs.title: Step-by-Step Process
docs.text:
1. Open Classification Tab
  2. Tap the camera icon (📷) in the bottom navigation

  3. You'll see the classification screen with action buttons

  4. Capture or Select Image

  5. Camera: Tap the camera button to take a new photo
  6. Gallery: Tap the gallery button to select an existing image

  7. Tips: Follow the photo guidelines above for best results

  8. Review Your Image

  9. The selected image will appear on screen
  10. Check that the mosquito is clearly visible and in focus

  11. Tap "Analyze" to start the identification process

  12. Wait for Analysis

  13. The AI model will process your image (usually 1-3 seconds)
  14. A progress indicator shows the analysis is in progress

  15. Processing happens entirely on your device

  16. Review Results

  17. Species name (scientific and common names)
  18. Confidence score (percentage)
  19. Processing time
  20. Associated disease information## U nderstanding Results

docs.title: Confidence Scores
docs.text:
The confidence score indicates how certain the AI model is about the identification:

  • 90-100%: Very High Confidence - Highly reliable identification
  • 70-89%: High Confidence - Reliable identification with good certainty
  • 50-69%: Moderate Confidence - Reasonable identification, consider additional verification
  • Below 50%: Low Confidence - Uncertain identification, may need better photo

docs.title: Species Information
docs.text:
Each identification result includes:

  • Scientific Name: The official taxonomic name (e.g., "Aedes aegypti")
  • Common Name: The widely used common name (e.g., "Yellow Fever Mosquito")
  • Description: Physical characteristics and identifying features
  • Habitat: Where this species typically lives and breeds
  • Distribution: Geographic regions where the species is found

docs.title: Disease Risk Information
docs.text:
For species that transmit diseases, you'll see:

  • Disease List: Diseases this species can transmit
  • Risk Level: Visual indicators of disease transmission potential
  • Prevention Tips: How to protect yourself from this species
  • Medical Information: Symptoms and treatment information for associated diseases

docs.title: When Results Seem Incorrect
docs.text:
If the identification doesn't seem right:

  1. Check Photo Quality: Ensure your photo meets the guidelines above
  2. Try Different Angles: Take additional photos from different perspectives
  3. Better Lighting: Retake the photo with improved lighting conditions
  4. Compare Features: Use the species gallery to compare visual features
  5. Consult Experts: For critical identifications, consult with entomologists

docs.title: Multiple Photos
docs.text: For best results, consider taking several photos: - Different angles (top, side, close-up) - Various lighting conditions - Multiple specimens if available - Compare results across photos

docs.title: Challenging Scenarios
docs.text:
Some situations make identification more difficult:

Damaged Specimens - Missing body parts reduce accuracy - Try to capture undamaged areas clearly - Focus on remaining identifying features

Similar Species - Some species look very similar - Pay attention to confidence scores - Use additional identifying features from the gallery - Consider geographic location

Poor Photo Conditions - Blurry images significantly reduce accuracy - Dark or overexposed photos are problematic - Motion blur from moving mosquitoes - Retake photos when conditions improve

docs.title: For Researchers and Citizen Scientists
docs.text:
Documentation - Record location, date, and time of collection - Note environmental conditions - Take multiple photos of each specimen - Keep detailed field notes

Quality Control - Always review confidence scores - Cross-reference with species gallery information - Verify geographic distribution matches your location - Consider seasonal activity patterns

Data Contribution - Submit high-quality observations to the research database - Include accurate location information - Add relevant notes about behavior or habitat - Contribute to scientific understanding

docs.title: For Public Health Awareness
docs.text:
Disease Prevention Focus - Pay special attention to disease-vector species - Learn to recognize dangerous species in your area - Understand seasonal activity patterns - Know when to seek medical attention

Community Education - Share knowledge with family and community - Report unusual species or activity patterns - Support local mosquito control efforts - Promote awareness of mosquito-borne diseases

docs.title: App Performance
docs.text:
• Slow Processing: Ensure sufficient device memory is available
  • App Crashes: Restart the app and try with a smaller image
  • Model Not Loading: Check that you have sufficient storage space

docs.title: Photo Issues
docs.text:
• Blurry Results: Use better lighting and steady hands
  • No Detection: Ensure the mosquito is clearly visible in the frame
  • Wrong Species: Try different angles and lighting conditions

docs.title: Technical Problems
docs.text:
• Camera Not Working: Check camera permissions in device settings
  • Gallery Access: Verify photo library permissions
  • Storage Issues: Free up device storage space

For additional help, see our Troubleshooting Guide or contact support.

docs.title: Professional Use
docs.text:
• Use macro lenses for detailed close-up photography
  • Consider using a microscope with camera attachment
  • Maintain consistent lighting setups for multiple specimens
  • Document metadata for scientific publications

docs.title: Field Work
docs.text:
• Carry a portable light source for consistent illumination
  • Use a white background card for better contrast
  • Take photos immediately after collection for best quality
  • Consider environmental factors that affect mosquito appearance

Remember: CulicidaeLab is a powerful tool for mosquito identification, but it works best when combined with good photography techniques and scientific knowledge. The more you practice, the better your results will become!

docs.title: Troubleshooting Guide
docs.text: This guide helps you resolve common issues you might encounter while using CulicidaeLab. Find solutions to technical problems, performance issues, and feature-specific challenges.

docs.title: App Won't Start or Crashes
docs.text:
Symptoms: App closes immediately, won't open, or crashes during startup

Solutions: 1. Restart the App: Close completely and reopen 2. Restart Device: Power off and on your phone/tablet 3. Check Storage: Ensure at least 500MB free space 4. Update App: Install latest version from app store 5. Clear Cache: Clear app cache in device settings

Android Specific: - Go to Settings > Apps > CulicidaeLab > Storage > Clear Cache - If problem persists, try "Clear Data" (will reset app settings)

iOS Specific: - Delete and reinstall the app if other solutions don't work - Check iOS version compatibility (requires iOS 12.0+)

docs.title: Classification Not Working
docs.text:
Symptoms: Camera won't open, photos won't analyze, or results don't appear

Immediate Fixes: 1. Check Permissions: Ensure camera and photo access are enabled 2. Restart App: Close and reopen CulicidaeLab 3. Try Different Image: Use a clearer, well-lit photo 4. Check Storage: Free up device storage space 5. Wait for Model: Allow time for AI model to load on first use

docs.title: Gallery or Disease Info Won't Load
docs.text:
Symptoms: Empty screens, loading indicators that don't finish, or error messages

Solutions: 1. Check Internet: Ensure stable internet connection for initial data download 2. Wait for Loading: Initial data download may take 1-2 minutes 3. Restart App: Close and reopen if loading seems stuck 4. Clear Cache: Clear app cache to refresh data 5. Update App: Ensure you have the latest version

docs.title: Camera Won't Open
docs.text:
Problem: Camera button doesn't work or shows error

Check Permissions: - Android: Settings > Apps > CulicidaeLab > Permissions > Camera (Enable) - iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera > CulicidaeLab (Enable)

Other Solutions: - Close other apps using the camera - Restart the device - Check if camera works in other apps - Update the app to latest version

docs.title: Photos Are Blurry or Poor Quality
docs.text:
Problem: Images are unclear, making identification difficult

Photography Tips: - Lighting: Use bright, natural light - Distance: Get closer to the mosquito while maintaining focus - Stability: Hold device steady or use a tripod - Focus: Tap on the mosquito to focus before taking photo - Background: Use plain, contrasting background

Technical Solutions: - Clean camera lens - Check if camera focus is working in other apps - Try different camera modes if available - Ensure adequate lighting conditions

docs.title: Gallery Photos Won't Select
docs.text:
Problem: Can't select existing photos from device gallery

Permission Check: - Android: Settings > Apps > CulicidaeLab > Permissions > Storage/Photos - iOS: Settings > Privacy & Security > Photos > CulicidaeLab

Other Fixes: - Restart the app - Try selecting different photo formats (JPEG works best) - Check if photos are stored locally (not just in cloud) - Ensure photos aren't corrupted## AI Model and Classification Issues

docs.title: Model Won't Load
docs.text:
Problem: "Model not loaded" error or classification doesn't start

Solutions: 1. Wait for Loading: Model loading can take 30-60 seconds on first launch 2. Check Storage: Ensure at least 200MB free space for model files 3. Restart App: Close completely and reopen 4. Check Platform: Ensure you're using Android or iOS (not supported on web/desktop) 5. Update App: Install latest version with model improvements

Memory Issues: - Close other apps to free RAM - Restart device if memory is very low - Consider device upgrade if consistently problematic

docs.title: Classification Results Seem Wrong
docs.text:
Problem: AI identifies wrong species or gives low confidence

Photo Quality Check: - Ensure mosquito fills most of the frame - Check that image is sharp and well-focused - Verify good lighting without harsh shadows - Make sure entire mosquito is visible

Verification Steps: 1. Compare with Gallery: Check species images in gallery 2. Try Multiple Photos: Take several photos from different angles 3. Check Geographic Range: Verify species occurs in your location 4. Consider Alternatives: Look at other high-confidence results

docs.title: Slow Classification Performance
docs.text:
Problem: Analysis takes very long or appears stuck

Performance Optimization: - Close Background Apps: Free up device memory - Restart App: Fresh start can improve performance - Reduce Image Size: Use smaller images if possible - Check Device Temperature: Allow device to cool if overheated - Update App: Newer versions may have performance improvements

Device Considerations: - Older devices may process more slowly - Ensure device meets minimum requirements - Consider upgrading device for better performance

docs.title: Map Won't Load
docs.text:
Problem: Mosquito activity map shows errors or won't display

Network Troubleshooting: 1. Check Internet: Ensure stable Wi-Fi or cellular connection 2. Try Different Network: Switch between Wi-Fi and cellular 3. Restart Router: Reset Wi-Fi connection 4. Check Firewall: Ensure app isn't blocked by network security 5. Wait and Retry: Server may be temporarily unavailable

docs.title: Observation Submission Fails
docs.text:
Problem: Can't submit mosquito observations to research database

Submission Troubleshooting: - Check Internet: Stable connection required for submission - Verify Location: Ensure location services are enabled - Complete Required Fields: Fill all mandatory information - Try Later: Server may be busy, try again in a few minutes - Check App Version: Update to latest version

docs.title: Language Changes Don't Apply
docs.text:
Problem: App doesn't switch to selected language

Language Fixes: 1. Restart App: Close completely and reopen 2. Check Device Language: Ensure device supports selected language 3. Clear Cache: Clear app cache and restart 4. Reinstall App: Delete and reinstall if problem persists 5. Update App: Ensure latest version with language improvements

docs.title: App Runs Slowly
docs.text:
Problem: Laggy interface, slow responses, or delayed actions

Performance Solutions: - Free Memory: Close other running apps - Restart Device: Clear system memory - Clear Cache: Remove temporary files - Free Storage: Delete unnecessary files to free space - Update App: Install performance improvements

Device Optimization: - Keep at least 1GB free storage - Restart device regularly - Update device operating system - Remove unused apps

docs.title: Storage Space Warnings
docs.text:
Problem: Device shows low storage warnings

Storage Management: 1. Delete Unused Apps: Remove apps you don't use 2. Clear Photo/Video Cache: Remove old media files 3. Move Files to Cloud: Use cloud storage for photos/videos 4. Clear App Caches: Clear cache for multiple apps 5. Use Storage Analyzer: Find and remove large files

CulicidaeLab Specific: - App uses approximately 300MB when fully loaded - Model files are cached locally for offline use - Gallery images are cached for better performance

docs.title: Android Issues
docs.text:
App Permissions Reset: - Android may reset permissions after updates - Manually re-enable camera, storage, and location permissions - Check "Auto-start" permissions for background model loading

Battery Optimization: - Disable battery optimization for CulicidaeLab - Go to Settings > Battery > Battery Optimization > CulicidaeLab > Don't Optimize

Storage Access Framework: - If gallery access fails, try using "Files" app to select photos - Clear storage permissions and re-grant them

docs.title: iOS Issues
docs.text:
App Transport Security: - Ensure iOS version supports required security protocols - Update iOS if map or network features don't work

Background App Refresh: - Enable Background App Refresh for CulicidaeLab - Settings > General > Background App Refresh > CulicidaeLab

iCloud Photo Library: - If photos won't select, ensure they're downloaded locally - Settings > Photos > Download and Keep Originals

docs.title: Complete App Reset
docs.text:
If multiple issues persist, try a complete reset:

  1. Export Data: Save any important observations or notes
  2. Clear All Data:
  3. Android: Settings > Apps > CulicidaeLab > Storage > Clear Data
  4. iOS: Delete and reinstall app
  5. Restart Device: Power cycle your device
  6. Reinstall App: Download fresh copy from app store
  7. Reconfigure: Set up permissions and preferences again

docs.title: Diagnostic Information
docs.text: When contacting support, provide: - Device model and operating system version - CulicidaeLab app version - Specific error messages - Steps to reproduce the problem - Screenshots of issues (if applicable)

docs.title: Factory Reset Considerations
docs.text: As a last resort for persistent device-wide issues: - Back up all important data first - Factory reset may resolve deep system conflicts - Reinstall apps and restore data carefully - Consider professional device support

docs.title: In-App Support
docs.text:
• Check for help icons (ℹ️) throughout the app
  • Look for tooltips and contextual help
  • Review app notifications for guidance

docs.title: Community Resources
docs.text:

  • Social media communities
  • Educational institution support

docs.title: Professional Support
docs.text:
• Contact app developers through official channels
  • Report bugs through app store reviews
  • Reach out via official website or email

docs.title: Emergency Situations
docs.text:
For medical emergencies related to mosquito-borne diseases: - Contact local emergency services immediately - Don't rely solely on app information for urgent medical decisions - Consult healthcare professionals for medical concerns

Remember: Most issues can be resolved with simple solutions like restarting the app or checking permissions. If problems persist, don't hesitate to seek help from the support resources listed above.

For frequently asked questions, see our FAQ Guide.

docs.title: Using the Mosquito Gallery
docs.text: The CulicidaeLab gallery provides a comprehensive visual reference for mosquito species, helping you learn about different species and their characteristics.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Mosquito Gallery is your gateway to exploring the world of mosquitoes. It contains detailed information about epidemiologically significant mosquito species, focusing on those that can transmit diseases to humans.

docs.title: What You'll Find
docs.text:
• Visual Species Guide: High-quality images of mosquito species
  • Scientific Information: Taxonomic details and physical descriptions
  • Habitat Data: Where each species lives and breeds
  • Disease Associations: Which diseases each species can transmit
  • Geographic Distribution: Where species are found worldwide

docs.title: Accessing the Gallery
docs.text:
1. Tap the mosquito icon (🦟) in the bottom navigation bar
  2. The gallery will load with a grid view of species cards
  3. Use the search bar at the top to find specific species

docs.title: Gallery Layout
docs.text: The gallery uses a two-column grid layout showing: - Species Image: High-quality photograph of the mosquito - Scientific Name: Overlaid on the image - Common Name: Below the image in bold text - Habitat Information: Brief habitat description - Disease Count: Number of diseases the species can transmit

docs.title: Search Functionality
docs.text:
The search feature helps you quickly find specific species:

Search by Name - Type scientific names (e.g., "Aedes aegypti") - Search common names (e.g., "Yellow Fever Mosquito") - Partial matches work (e.g., "Aedes" shows all Aedes species)

Search Tips - Search is case-insensitive - Use partial words for broader results - Clear search with the X button - Results update as you type

docs.title: Species Information Cards
docs.text: Each species card provides essential information at a glance:

docs.title: Visual Elements
docs.text:
• High-Quality Image: Professional photograph showing key identifying features
  • Scientific Name Overlay: Clearly displayed on the image
  • Disease Warning Icon: Red warning icon if the species transmits diseases

docs.title: Information Display
docs.text:
• Common Name: User-friendly name in your selected language
  • Habitat: Brief description of preferred breeding and living environments
  • Disease Vector Count: Number of diseases this species can transmit
  • Visual Indicators: Color-coded elements for quick recognition

docs.title: Interaction
docs.text:
• Tap to View Details: Tap any card to open the detailed species page
  • Visual Feedback: Cards highlight when tapped
  • Smooth Navigation: Seamless transition to detail screens

docs.title: Detailed Species Pages
docs.text: Tapping on a species card opens a comprehensive detail page with:

docs.title: Species Overview
docs.text:
• Large Image: Full-screen view of the species
  • Scientific Classification: Complete taxonomic information
  • Common Names: Multiple common names in different languages
  • Physical Description: Detailed morphological characteristics

docs.title: Habitat and Distribution
docs.text:
• Preferred Habitats: Detailed breeding site preferences
  • Geographic Range: Countries and regions where found
  • Environmental Conditions: Climate and seasonal preferences
  • Urban vs. Rural: Habitat type preferences

docs.title: Disease Information
docs.text:
• Associated Diseases: Complete list of diseases this species can transmit
  • Transmission Details: How diseases are transmitted
  • Risk Assessment: Relative importance as a disease vector
  • Prevention Methods: How to protect against this species

docs.title: Additional Information
docs.text:
• Behavior Patterns: Activity times and feeding preferences
  • Life Cycle: Development stages and timing
  • Control Methods: How this species is managed
  • Research Notes: Recent scientific findings## Learning Features

docs.title: Educational Use
docs.text:
The gallery serves as an educational resource for:

Students and Educators - Visual learning aids for entomology courses - Comparative morphology studies - Disease vector education - Public health awareness training

Healthcare Professionals - Disease vector identification - Risk assessment for different regions - Patient education materials - Epidemiological reference

Researchers and Scientists - Species verification and confirmation - Morphological comparisons - Distribution mapping - Literature reference

docs.title: Comparative Analysis
docs.text:
Use the gallery to compare similar species:

  1. Open Multiple Species: Navigate between similar species
  2. Compare Features: Look for distinguishing characteristics
  3. Note Differences: Pay attention to size, color, and pattern variations
  4. Geographic Overlap: Check if species occur in the same regions

docs.title: Filtering and Sorting
docs.text:
While browsing the gallery, you can:

Filter by Disease Risk - Focus on species that transmit specific diseases - Identify high-risk vectors in your area - Understand disease transmission patterns

Sort by Relevance - Geographic relevance to your location - Disease importance - Alphabetical order - Recent additions to the database

docs.title: Offline Access
docs.text: The gallery works offline once loaded: - Cached Images: Species images are stored locally - Offline Information: All text content available without internet - Search Functionality: Search works offline - Smooth Performance: No loading delays for cached content

docs.title: Multi-language Support
docs.text: Gallery content is available in multiple languages: - Species Names: Scientific names remain consistent, common names translated - Descriptions: All text content in your selected language - Habitat Information: Localized environmental descriptions - Disease Names: Disease names in local language

docs.title: Verification Process
docs.text:
After getting identification results, use the gallery to:

  1. Cross-Reference: Compare your photo with gallery images
  2. Verify Features: Check if identifying features match
  3. Confirm Distribution: Ensure the species occurs in your area
  4. Assess Confidence: Use visual comparison to validate AI results

docs.title: Learning Identification
docs.text:
Improve your identification skills by:

Study Similar Species - Learn distinguishing features between similar species - Understand geographic distribution patterns - Recognize seasonal variations - Practice visual identification

Understand Morphology - Learn mosquito anatomy and terminology - Recognize key identifying features - Understand sexual dimorphism (male vs. female differences) - Appreciate size and scale variations

docs.title: Common Problems
docs.text:
Images Not Loading - Check internet connection for initial download - Ensure sufficient storage space - Restart the app if images appear corrupted - Clear app cache if problems persist

Search Not Working - Check spelling of search terms - Try partial words or alternative names - Clear search and try again - Restart app if search becomes unresponsive

Slow Performance - Close other apps to free memory - Restart the app - Check available storage space - Update to the latest app version

docs.title: Optimization Tips
docs.text:
Improve Performance - Allow the app to cache images for offline use - Keep the app updated for performance improvements - Ensure adequate device storage space - Close unnecessary background apps

Better Experience - Use the app in good lighting for better image viewing - Rotate device for better image viewing when needed - Use zoom gestures to examine details closely - Take advantage of offline capabilities

docs.title: Data Quality
docs.text: Help improve the gallery by: - Reporting incorrect information - Suggesting additional species for inclusion - Providing feedback on image quality - Contributing high-quality photographs

docs.title: Community Engagement
docs.text:
• Share interesting species discoveries
  • Participate in citizen science projects
  • Contribute to species distribution mapping
  • Support mosquito research initiatives

The Mosquito Gallery is more than just a reference tool—it's your gateway to understanding the complex world of mosquitoes and their role in public health. Whether you're a student, researcher, healthcare professional, or curious citizen, the gallery provides the visual and scientific information you need to identify and understand these important insects.

For more information about specific features or troubleshooting, see our FAQ or Troubleshooting Guide.
